clue.text: Let me tell you what my tutor will do

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a phrase used to insist that a prediction will come true
second meaning, read literally: a tutor grades the student's written essay

explanation.surface: A student warns a friend of what the tutor is going to do next.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading: a tutor marks the words the student writes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is said to stress a warning or prediction, much like 'believe me' or 'take it from me'.

clue.text: Market not stocking right floor-covering

indicators.note: a shop not stocking an item lacks it, so one letter is left out of the word

parts.note: a mart is a market
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A shop that sells no proper rugs or carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat is a small piece of material laid on a floor, a simple kind of floor covering.

clue.text: City apparently offering a good deal?

definitions.text: City apparently offering a good deal?

parts.words: City apparently offering a good deal?
parts.note: surface reading: a town where shoppers find bargains
setter's reading; the city's name looks like that invented phrase

explanation.surface: A city where shopping seems to give good value.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire. Split as RIP ON, it reads as the reverse of a rip-off, which is a swindle; hence 'apparently'.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a genuine English city whose name looks like the opposite of a slang term for a swindle.

clue.text: This chap's a husband mostly supported by the wife

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
in a down clue something supported sits on top, so this part comes before what follows

parts.note: a mate is a spouse, here a husband
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A man described as a husband kept by his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTHEW is MAT (MATE without its last letter) above THE W. 'This chap' points at the answer as a man's name; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew is a man's given name, so it can stand for some particular chap.

clue.text: Narrow victory keeping father excited

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jump about out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A father gets worked up over a team's victory by the slimmest margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Narrow victory' looks like one phrase meaning a close win; in fact 'Narrow' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wafer-thin is extremely slender, as thin as a wafer biscuit, so it is very narrow.

clue.text: One's brought in support for later exam

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is drafted in to help a student retaking a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second sitting of an examination taken after failing the first, so a later exam.

clue.text: Second deliveryman forgetting one item of kitchen equipment

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: someone forgetting a thing leaves it behind, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a courier delivers parcels and letters
I is the Roman numeral one, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A second delivery driver leaves behind one of the kitchen items.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is an abrasive pad used for scrubbing pans, a common piece of kitchen kit.

clue.text: Lady's celebration cut short

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

explanation.surface: A woman's party ends early.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is an informal word for a girl or woman, a casual equivalent of lady.

clue.text: Soldier unexpectedly reading about uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up, so the short word turns round
something unexpected does not follow the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A soldier is caught off guard reading about a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' looks like the subject of the soldier's reading; it only tells you to turn RE upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenadier is a soldier, originally one who threw grenades, now a member of a guards regiment.

clue.text: It's connected to your point of view

definitions.text: It's connected to your point of view

parts.words: It's connected to your point of view
parts.note: surface reading: something related to your opinion
setter's reading: the literal place you look from, joined by a straight path to whatever you are looking at

explanation.surface: Something tied up with your opinion on a matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point of view' reads as an opinion, but here it is literally the spot your eyes are at, and the answer is the straight path from it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the imaginary straight track from an observer's eye to the thing seen, so it runs from where you view.

clue.text: Legal officers' suggestions about employees

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: tips are suggestions or pieces of advice
a firm's employees are its staff

explanation.surface: Lawyers make proposals concerning their workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is a sheriff's officer or court official in British law. The definition is possessive, 'Legal officers' suggestions', with the 's read as 'is' in a plural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipstaffs are court officers who make arrests and enforce orders, named after the metal-tipped staff they once carried.

clue.text: Energy company backing a new main

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
Co is the abbreviation for company
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A power firm supports a fresh water main or gas main.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' suggests a pipe; it is the old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the high seas, so it means the ocean.

clue.text: Appear lustful with that woman? The animal!

parts.note: to pant after someone is to show lust or longing
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation about a man ogling a woman: the beast!
explanation.walkthrough: 'The animal!' sounds like an insult to the lecher, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A panther is a big cat, a leopard or jaguar, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Tie-breaker's fine stimulant effect

parts.note: a fine is a penalty
the kick of a drink or drug is its stimulating effect

explanation.surface: A neckwear snapper gets a jolt from a pleasing pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie-breaker' looks like someone who breaks neckties; it is a way to settle a drawn match.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn football matches are often settled by a shoot-out of penalty kicks, so each one breaks a tie.

clue.text: Activity linked to rent causing a storm

parts.note: rent means torn, as in a rent garment
ado is fuss or bustling activity

explanation.surface: A dispute over rent payments stirs up a furore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord; here it is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm, so it is a kind of storm.

clue.text: Never showing radio announcer's skill?

indicators.note: on the radio words are only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: know-how is practical skill

explanation.surface: A radio presenter who never displays any talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect or informal word meaning in no way at all, so it serves as never.

clue.text: Workers beat leader of directors? That's an inversion!

parts.note: hands are manual workers
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Staff thrash the boss of the board, a complete reversal of roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inversion' suggests the overturned hierarchy; it is the gymnast's upside-down position.
explanation.definitionFit: A handstand turns the body upside down, balanced on the hands, so it is an inversion.

clue.text: Greeting to right girl not having consistent effect

parts.note: hi is a greeting
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Saying hello to the right girl does not always work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hit-or-miss is erratic, succeeding only some of the time, so its results are not consistent.

clue.text: Article is memorable, depicting rural areas

parts.note: the definite article
something memorable sticks in the mind

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature that lingers in the mind describes the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a piece of writing; it is the grammatical word THE.
explanation.definitionFit: The sticks is an informal term for remote countryside far from towns, hence rural areas.

clue.text: Be keen to go wandering, needing such a forecast?

definitions.note: the answer describes the kind of forecast, so it fits as an adjective before it

parts.note: to long for something is to be keen on it
to range is to roam or wander

explanation.surface: A keen rambler wants to know the weather well ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-range forecast predicts the weather weeks ahead, the sort a walker planning a trip wants.

clue.text: About to get striker for return game

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a match is struck to light it, so it is a striker

explanation.surface: A team is about to sign a centre-forward for the return fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' suggests a footballer; it is something struck to make a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, a return game after the first.

clue.text: Second show of affection overcomes resistance and sign of indifference

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: to overcome is to come over and around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a hug is a show of affection
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A second cuddle wins over someone reluctant who was showing no interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the shoulders in a shrug is a gesture showing you do not care, so it signals indifference.

clue.text: Useful gadget that could be bought for a tanner?

definitions.text: Useful gadget that could be bought for a tanner?

parts.words: Useful gadget that could be bought for a tanner?
parts.note: surface reading: a cheap gadget priced at sixpence, since a tanner was the old British sixpenny coin
setter's reading: a person who tans, wanting a bronzed skin without real sunshine

explanation.surface: A handy device you could once buy for sixpence.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was slang for the pre-1971 British sixpence coin, which makes the clue sound like a bargain price; really it is someone after a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: This lamp gives off ultraviolet light that browns the skin, so a person seeking a tan would buy one.

clue.text: Cover showing ox eating prepared mash

indicators.note: what is eaten goes inside the eater, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired Tibetan ox

indicators.note: something prepared is made up or worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A picture on a cover shows an ox eating its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mash is a mix of grain fed to livestock, so the surface paints a farmyard scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women to hide the face, so it is a cover.

clue.text: Overturned drink surrounding one rug

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom up
surrounding means going around, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: milk is a drink
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A spilt drink soaks a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilim is a flat-woven carpet from Turkey or Persia, a kind of rug.

clue.text: Ready to come in drunk later today

indicators.note: what comes in goes inside, so one word enters the other

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk
on can mean ready to go, as in 'you're on'

explanation.surface: Someone expects to stagger home drunk this evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight is the evening of the present day, so it is later today.

clue.text: Director of university introduced to French writer

indicators.note: something introduced into a thing is put inside it, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: André Gide was a French novelist and Nobel laureate
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A university head is presented to a French author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Director of university' reads as one title, a vice-chancellor say; 'Director' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide shows the way and steers others, so it is one who directs.

clue.text: I doze off before end of it? That's badly judged

parts.note: taken as written
to nap is to doze off briefly

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone admits nodding off before a film or talk finishes, a poor call.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inapt is unsuitable for the occasion, so a remark or choice made poorly is inapt.

clue.text: Development of vital cure could be rewarding

indicators.note: a development changes a thing into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A drug company expects a life-saving remedy to make it rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucrative venture brings in plenty of money, so it is financially rewarding.

clue.text: Characters repeatedly seen in summer in German city

wordplay.note: the letter appearing twice in a row in summer is M

explanation.surface: Faces that keep turning up in a German town during the warm months.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters have spelt names: M is 'em', so the double M of summer is ems. Bad Ems is a German spa town on the River Lahn.
explanation.definitionFit: Ems, or Bad Ems, is a spa town in western Germany, famous for its mineral springs.

clue.text: Child, amiable, but not offering name

indicators.note: not offering something means holding it back, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a kind person is amiable
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A friendly youngster who will not say who they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid is an informal word for a child, from the word for a young goat.

clue.text: Man hopes man is smitten with love

indicators.note: smitten means struck hard, and struck letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A man hopes another man has fallen for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smitten with love' reads as besotted; 'smitten' alone stirs the letters and love adds an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is the scientific name of the human species, so it is Man in the sense of mankind.
